identity.description: Fully parametric accelerated-failure-time model: covariates multiplicatively rescale survival TIME (exp(coef) is a time ratio — 'members with X last 1.3x longer'), vs Cox's hazard-ratio reading. Buys extrapolation beyond the observed window and absolute time predictions by assuming Weibull-distributed lifetimes.

consumes.note: the (duration, event-indicator) pair carried as two columns alongside the covariate matrix — same regime as cox_ph

emits.note: closed-form Weibull S(t|x) — smooth, defined for ALL t including beyond the observed window (the extrapolation the assumption buys)
closed-form ABSOLUTE hazard h(t|x) — a full time-varying hazard, not just Cox's relative-risk ranking against an unspecified baseline

log TIME-ratios with CIs: exp(coef) multiplies survival time (acceleration factor) — interpretation and sign convention are the OPPOSITE of Cox's hazard ratios; a positive coef here means LONGER survival
predicted median/expected survival time per row — the absolute 'when' number Cox's partial hazard cannot give without a baseline estimate

penalizer.note: elastic-net strength on the regression coefficients; stabilizes under collinearity/few events

ancillary.note: when true, the Weibull shape parameter rho is ALSO regressed on covariates — heteroskedastic acceleration (covariates change hazard shape, not just scale)

invariances.why: coefficients are per-unit log time-ratios in a log-linear location model; unscaled features give incomparable magnitudes and unstable Newton steps
log(T) is modeled as linear in covariates; a monotone covariate transform changes the fit
the parametric likelihood has no missing-value handling — NaN covariate rows are dropped or must be imputed

assumes WEIBULL lifetimes — the full distribution, a strictly stronger claim than Cox's PH: hazard must be monotone (rising or falling per rho, never bathtub/hump-shaped). Mechanism note: Weibull is the unique family satisfying BOTH AFT (covariates rescale time, S(t|x)=S0(t*exp(-x'b))) and PH — so Cox and Weibull AFT agree in ranking here and diverge only in absolute-time claims
the full parametric likelihood extracts more per event than Cox's partial likelihood — usable at low event counts IF the Weibull form holds; the assumption is doing the work the data cannot
the closed parametric form extends S(t|x) beyond the last observed time — the trait KM/Cox lack, and the principal reason to pay the distributional assumption

featureStats.why: THE commit-survival stat: the right-censored fraction is what makes a survival model necessary vs a fixed-window classifier
effective sample size is the number of events; few events flags a penalizer and wide CIs — though the parametric likelihood degrades more gracefully than Cox's partial likelihood

under Weibull, log(-log S(t)) = rho*log t - rho*log lambda is LINEAR in log t — plot it from the KM curve; curvature is direct evidence against the assumed distribution and routes toward log-normal/log-logistic AFT or RSF

modelMetrics.why: the survival-native ranking metric (Harrell's C) — with the ceiling caveat: near-deterministic durations inflate C toward 1, so report it alongside the censoring context, not as a lone scoreboard number
the full likelihood makes AIC comparable across parametric survival fits — the honest instrument for choosing Weibull vs log-normal vs log-logistic, which pure ranking (C-index) cannot distinguish

edgeCases.behavior: likelihood carries no event information — scale/shape unidentifiable
Weibull support is strictly t > 0; log(t) undefined — fit raises
Weibull cannot represent it — systematically biased curve and time-ratios
edgeCases.note: route to log-normal/log-logistic AFT (hump) or RSF (arbitrary shape); detected via the loglog-linearity stat

edgeCases.behavior: coefficient diverges, Newton fails to converge

driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: (duration,event) columns split from the matrix; predict maps to predict_survival_function / predict_median / predict_expectation / predict_hazard

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling; unimputed rows are silently dropped, biasing the likelihood
log/Yeo-Johnson of skewed covariates improves the log-linear location fit
coefficients are per-unit log time-ratios; standardization makes acceleration factors comparable and the Newton solver stable
categoricals must be design-encoded before entering the parametric likelihood
